body.title: perf: mark lazy event handler factory as side-effect-free
body.body:
Allow bundlers to remove unused `defineLazyEventHandler()` calls.

Repro bundle sizes with H3 `2.0.8` and Rolldown `1.2.14`:

| Fixture | Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Unused lazy handler | Minified | 14,140 B | 1,214 B |
| Unused lazy handler | Gzip | 5,107 B | 714 B |

[Reproduction](https://github.com/onmax/repros/tree/repro/h3-pure-lazy), Node `24.21.0` and pnpm `11.28.5`:

```sh
git clone --depth 1 --branch repro/h3-pure-lazy https://github.com/onmax/repros.git h3-repro
cd h3-repro
node verify.mjs
```

body.title: fix(response): keep `iterable` streaming past skipped values
body.body:
`iterable()` drops `undefined` values and values the serializer returns `undefined` for, but the `pull()` call that drops one resolves without enqueuing anything. `ReadableStream` only calls `pull()` again if another read arrived while it was running, so a pending read can be left unanswered and the response never finishes. Consecutive or trailing skips can trigger it on both web and node:

```ts
iterable(["a", undefined, "b", undefined]); // hangs, expected "ab"
iterable(["a", "skip", "skip", "b"], { serializer }); // serializer returns undefined for "skip"; hangs, expected "ab"
```

`pull()` now keeps reading until it enqueues a chunk or the iterator is done. Values that serialize to a chunk are handled as before.

- Ran: `pnpm vitest run test/iterable.test.ts`: both new tests time out on `main` in web and node (4 failed, 38 passed) and pass with the fix (42 passed).
- Ran: `pnpm vitest run --coverage`: 73 files, 3134 passed, 51 skipped.
- Checked: `pnpm typecheck`, `oxlint .` and `pnpm build` pass; `oxfmt --check` is clean on the changed files.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Response streams continue past values that produce no output, allowing later values to be delivered.
  * Values that cannot be serialized are omitted without interrupting the remaining stream.
  * Streams close when iteration finishes, including when the final value has no serializable output.
  * After cancellation, streams stop reading additional values and do not serialize values that arrive afterward.

body.title: fix(node): don't listen for close/error after a synchronous next()
body.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

Resolves #1610

### ❓ Type of change

- [x] 🐞 Bug fix (a non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

### 📚 Description

`callNodeListener` runs the handler first and only then registers `res.once("close", next)` and `res.once("error", next)`. A Node middleware that calls `next()` synchronously has already run `next`, and its `res.off(...)` found nothing to remove. The listeners are added afterwards and never removed. Each such layer leaves one `close` and one `error` listener on the response, so with more than 10 layers Node prints `MaxListenersExceededWarning`, as in the issue.

`next` now sets a `called` flag, and the listeners are registered only if the handler returned without calling it. Everything else is unchanged:
- a middleware that calls `next()` later still has its listeners, so `close` or `error` still settles it;
- they are still removed when `next()` runs;
- a returned value still resolves the promise.

This is against `v1`, since the report is for 1.15.11. `main`'s rewritten Node adapter doesn't register these per-middleware listeners, so it doesn't need the change. PR #1028 touched the same ordering for hanging responses; this change only stops the late registration.

Test: in `test/app.test.ts`, 15 `fromNodeMiddleware((req, res, next) => next())` layers run before a final one that records `res.listenerCount("close")` and `("error")`. It expects `[0, 0]`, and on `v1` it fails. `vitest --run` passes all 356 tests (1 skipped), and `eslint`, `prettier -c` and `tsgo --noEmit` are clean (Node 22, offline).
